A Homeowner’s Guide to Understanding the Roof Inspection Process

25 February 2025 Roof Inspections

Your roof takes a beating here in Allentown. We see it all—snowy winters, heavy spring rains, summer heat, and strong winds in the fall. Over time, all that weather adds up. That’s why regular roof inspections aren’t just a good idea—they’re essential.

But if you’ve never had a professional roof inspection, you might not know what to expect. Don’t worry; you’re not alone. This roof inspection process guide breaks down the steps so you know exactly what happens and why it matters. Plus, we’ll share some expert insights from In The Light Roofing, a local team that’s been helping Allentown homeowners keep their roofs in shape for years.

Why roof inspections are so important

A roof might seem sturdy, but problems can sneak up on you. Shingles crack, flashing rusts, and leaks start small before causing big trouble. Inspections catch these issues early, which can save you thousands of dollars down the road.

Here’s why regular inspections matter:

    • Spot small problems early: Tiny cracks today can mean major leaks tomorrow.
  • Prevent water damage: Allentown’s heavy rains can find their way through the smallest openings.
  • Extend your roof’s lifespan: Routine care keeps your roof going strong for years.
  • Protect your home’s value: A well-maintained roof makes your home more attractive to buyers.

Think of a roof inspection like a doctor’s checkup. It’s about staying healthy, not just fixing issues when something breaks.

When should you schedule a roof inspection?

In Allentown, timing your roof inspections around the seasons helps catch damage early. Our temperature swings—from freezing nights to scorching afternoons—are tough on roofing materials.

Best times to schedule an inspection:

  • Spring: After winter snow and ice have melted, exposing potential damage.
  • Fall: Before winter hits, ensure your roof is ready for snow and ice.
  • After major storms: High winds, hail, or heavy rain can cause damage you won’t notice from the ground.
  • Before buying or selling a home: A roof inspection gives buyers confidence and sellers peace of mind.

If you notice water stains, missing shingles, or rising energy bills, don’t wait—schedule an inspection immediately.

Step 1. Ground-level inspection of the roof’s exterior

The first thing a roofer does is walk around your home and check the roof from the ground. This gives them a big-picture view of your roof’s condition and helps identify obvious damage.

What they look for:

  • Shingles that are missing, cracked, or curling
  • Sagging areas that may indicate structural issues
  • Moss, algae, or dark streaks, which suggest moisture problems
  • Granules collecting near downspouts, a sign of aging shingles

Allentown’s wet springs and humid summers often lead to moss growth, so professionals pay close attention to shaded areas.

Step 2. Closer inspection of the roof surface

Next, the roofer climbs up to take a closer look. This step is crucial because ground-level checks only reveal so much.

What they check during this step:

  • Shingle integrity, including cracks, curling, or missing pieces
  • Flashing around chimneys, vents, and skylights
  • The condition of roof valleys where water runoff is heaviest
  • Signs of hail damage, like dents or small holes

Hailstorms are becoming more common in the Lehigh Valley, so this part of the inspection helps catch damage early.

Step 3. Gutter and drainage system evaluation

Your gutters do more than just catch rainwater. They protect your home by directing water away from the roof and foundation. If they’re not working properly, your roof could pay the price.

The inspector will check:

  • Gutters for clogs, rust, or sagging
  • Downspouts for blockages that can cause water backup
  • Signs of water overflow, like staining on siding or fascia boards
  • Proper alignment and slope for efficient drainage

Keeping gutters clear is especially important in Allentown, where autumn leaves often clog the system.

Step 4. Attic inspection for hidden issues

Not all roof damage is visible from the outside. The attic often shows the first signs of trouble, like moisture or heat buildup.

What inspectors look for in the attic:

  • Water stains or damp insulation
  • Mold growth or musty smells
  • Sunlight peeking through the roofboards
  • Proper ventilation to prevent ice dams in winter

In Allentown’s cold months, poor attic ventilation can cause ice dams, which force water under shingles and into your home.

Step 5. Structural evaluation of the roof

A roof isn’t just shingles—it’s a complex structure that needs to stay level and strong. Inspectors assess the roof’s framework to catch any signs of sagging or shifting.

Structural warning signs:

  • Uneven or dipping rooflines
  • Cracked or warped rafters
  • Separation between roof and walls
  • Visible sagging along ridges or valleys

Allentown’s snowy winters add weight to roofs, so this step ensures your structure can handle future storms.

Step 6. Final inspection report and recommendations

After examining the roof, the inspector provides a detailed report of their findings. This document isn’t just technical jargon—it’s a clear explanation of what’s working, what needs fixing, and how urgent any issues might be.

The report typically includes:

  • Photos of damaged areas
  • A summary of potential problem spots
  • Recommended repairs or maintenance steps
  • Cost estimates and timeframes for necessary work

If repairs are needed, check out our Roof Inspections page to learn how we can help.

Tips to maintain your roof between inspections

You don’t have to wait for an inspection to take care of your roof. A little attention throughout the year goes a long way.

Simple maintenance steps:

  • Clean your gutters every spring and fall.
  • Trim tree branches that hang over the roof.
  • Check for missing shingles after storms.
  • Look for water stains in the attic regularly.
  • Schedule professional inspections twice a year.

Being proactive can save you from costly surprises.

Why local expertise matters for roof inspections

Roofing isn’t the same everywhere. Allentown’s weather creates specific challenges that roofers from other regions might not understand. Local roofing companies know what to look for and how to address issues caused by our distinct seasonal changes.

Why choose a local roofer like In The Light Roofing:

  • We understand Allentown’s freeze-thaw cycles and their impact on roofs.
  • We stay up to date with local building codes and permit requirements.
  • We use materials suited to Pennsylvania’s climate.

With years of experience in the community, we’ve helped countless homeowners stay ahead of roof problems. Visit our Roof Inspections page to learn more.

Conclusion

Understanding the roof inspection process guide helps you stay proactive with your home’s most important protective layer. From spotting damaged shingles to checking attic ventilation, each step ensures your roof stays in top shape. Regular inspections save money, extend your roof’s lifespan, and keep your family safe.

If you’re due for an inspection or have concerns about your roof, reach out to In The Light Roofing. Our team knows exactly what to look for and how to fix small problems before they become big ones. Visit our Roof Inspections page to schedule your inspection today.

Frequently asked questions

How often should I get my roof inspected?

Twice a year is ideal—once in spring and once in fall. Also, schedule an inspection after any severe storm.

What are common issues found during roof inspections?

Inspectors often find missing shingles, damaged flashing, clogged gutters, and water stains in the attic.

Can I check my roof myself?

You can do a basic ground-level check, but a professional inspection is more thorough and safer.

How long does a roof inspection take?

Most inspections take one to two hours, depending on your roof’s size and condition.

Does Allentown’s weather make roof inspections more important?

Yes. The freeze-thaw cycles, heavy snow, and seasonal storms put extra stress on roofs here.

Who should I call for a roof inspection in Allentown?

In The Light Roofing provides expert, local inspections to keep your roof in great condition.
